text: The guy in this story started an open relationship with a girl, but found himself wanting more. Now he doesn't know what to do since the girl said no. My girlfriend and I have been in a secret open relationship for a year now. Maybe in the first month she used the secret open relationship label as a way to do what she wants. I wasn't perfect either and I did go out in the clubs as well. The whole relationship started out as friends with benefits, but after like 6 months she has stopped going out in the club. She started asking me to come to her place. She knew I had a girlfriend outside her and she still wanted me to spend time with her. She wasn't with anyone and would mostly stay at home. She even told me she is jealous of my other girlfriend and after some time I asked her does she want a normal relationship. And she said no. She said she wasn't sure if she wants to give me false hope and she isn't sure if maybe the label of a relationship is tainted for her and that she loves me too much to limit me. Even after I told her it's what I wanted. And now I'm stuck in this position where I feel like she even distanced just a tiny bit because of me even suggesting it. What should I do? Ok, so in a nutshell. The guy had an open relationship. Now he wants the relationship to be quote-unquote normal. I suppose he means when they are exclusive to each other. But the girl says no. And now our guy doesn't know what to do. Look, most open relationships, situationships, friends with benefits, whatever you want to call them, end in one of two ways. Either you take them to the next level, for example, into the serious relationship. Or they just end. It is not something bad. You both hopefully had a great time, pleasant experience, and nice memories. From experience, this is how it normally works. You start seeing the girl casually, without any labels. And after about 2 months or say 10-15 meetings, emotions go to the peak. And most guys and girls start to develop real feelings. This is the moment when one of two people, and normally it is a girl, starts hinting on taking it to another level. Yes, it is a double standard, the same way that it is normally the guy who initiates the courtship process, it is normally the girl who initiates taking it to another level. So here you need to decide whether you actually want to take it to another level. For example, whether you want a serious relationship or not. Whether she is the right girl for you, whether it is the right time, and so on. Because afterwards, emotions cloud the mind and most guys simply lose their heads. Even if they saw the red flags, even if they knew it is a bad idea, they still end up going into the relationship. And then I receive the questions that I receive. In your case, it took longer, about a year to get to that point, which is a bit unusual, but same idea. So you see, you started to develop feelings, you actually talked to your girl about going into a normal relationship, she said no, well, that's it. Have some self-respect and walk away until it is too late and you also lose your head. This story should end at some point, right? So say thank you for this experience and go live your life. My advice, though, is that you need to cut the contact with this girl, because without that step, many guys would still find it hard to move on, even from open relationships.
